title: Contextual audit viewer: sample-based CSV/JSON export with cursor-aware pagination
creator: Sofia Ramos
body:
Problem:
The existing audit viewer export flows are vulnerable to long-running queries for large date ranges and high-cardinality filters. Customers and internal auditors need an export UX that provides reliable, resumable CSV/JSON downloads, preserves result ordering for forensic workflows, and respects RBAC v2 scoping without exposing partial rows.

Goal:
- Provide a console action to export search results (CSV or JSON) that: 1) streams results carefully to avoid OOM, 2) supports cursor-aware pagination for resumable exports, 3) offers sample-based preview and size estimates before full export, and 4) enforces RBAC/field-redaction at export time.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement long-term archival or S3 lifecycle management (separate infra work). It also does not change retention policies.

Acceptance criteria:
- Console "Export results" button toggles a modal with format (CSV/JSON), sampling preview (first 100 rows), and estimated size (rows/MB) based on query cardinality heuristics.
- Export backend accepts an export request and returns a resumable cursor token.
- Consumers can poll an export status endpoint to get progress and download link when ready.
- Exports stream data server-side to minimize memory; for CSV we use chunked transfer with periodic flushes and content-length omitted.
- RBAC v2 checks applied per-row and per-field before writing any output; any redacted fields must be marked with <REDACTED>.
- Exports are rate-limited per-organization and logged in audit events.
- Pagination uses opaque cursor tokens that encode query + server snapshot id; cursors are valid for 72 hours.

Design notes and constraints:
- Use existing audit-query service for result discovery; add a lightweight "export coordinator" lambda that orchestrates streaming tasks into signed temporary URLs (download tokens) hosted on the console CDN.
- Sampling preview must execute fast on large indexes; implement reservoir sampling on the query head to estimate unique user counts and bytes.
- For very large result sets (>100M rows) surface a warning and require explicit manager approval (console checkbox) to proceed.
- For CSV, follow RFC 4180 quoting rules; for JSON, produce newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON).

Links and artifacts:
- Design sketch (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/audit-export-flow
- PRD (Confluence): https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/6123456/Contextual+Audit+Export+PRD
- Spike notes (internal doc): https://docs.redwood.ai/spikes/audit-export-sampling
- Prototype backend spike repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-export-spike
comments: 2026-02-22 - Sofia Ramos: Initial triage done; prioritized after RBAC v2 rollout. Linked PRD and figma. Assigned to Marcus.
2026-02-24 - Marcus Liu: Completed API surface sketch. Suggest export coordinator service to avoid coupling with main query engine. Added dependency ENG-82011 for RBAC enforcement hooks.
2026-02-27 - Marcus Liu: Spike results: reservoir sampling gives <5% error on estimated row counts for 1M+ result sets and completes in ~300ms on prod cluster. See spike repo for benchmark scripts.
2026-03-03 - Eng Review: Reviewed streaming approach in RFC; Ops flagged need for per-org rate limiting and s3/presigned-url TTLs. Updated design notes.
2026-03-06 - Design (Anya Patel): Modal UX updated to show estimated completion time and manager-approval checkbox for >100M rows. Figma updated.

2026-03-09 - Marcus Liu: Implemented backend coordinator prototype: CSV streaming with chunk size 64KB, test export of 10M rows completed in staging (avg throughput 3.8k rows/s). Memory stayed <150MB. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2802
2026-03-11 - Security (Daniel Osei): Reviewed RBAC enforcement integration; requested explicit test vectors for field redaction and role permutations. Added security_review_required flag.
2026-03-12 - Marcus Liu: Addressed security tests; added audit events for export.start/export.complete/export.failed. Working on pagination token encryption.
decisions: Use NDJSON for JSON exports to simplify streaming and partial-consumption by downstream tools.
Opaque cursor tokens will embed a server snapshot id and be HMAC-signed; validity window set to 72 hours.
For RBAC field redaction we will apply transformations server-side and mark redacted fields as <REDACTED> to preserve schema for downstream parsers.
Sampling preview will use reservoir sampling on the query head to estimate unique counts and byte size; accept ~5% variance for performance gains.
